findings.reason: a worker implementing the section verbatim would write a literal missing test path and watch the fifth case store, then either report the section blocked or weaken the shared function to manufacture the refusal, both of which change what gets built.
findings.text: the fifth case ("an entry whose gate names a test file the repository does not hold is refused in the batch result") cannot be satisfied as written: `gate_population_patterns` (reckon/crew/node.py:1099-1111) keeps a token only when `_GATE_POPULATION_IS_A_SET` matches `[?*\[]`, so a literal `pytest tests/no_such_test.py` yields no pattern and `gate_population_finding` returns None; verified by direct call — `gate_population_patterns("pytest tests/test_missing.py")` → `[]`, `gate_population_finding` on a node whose gate is `pytest tests/does_not_exist_abc.py` → `None`, while the glob spelling `tests/does_not_exist_abc*.py` → `'gate-population'`. The fifth case therefore fails in the head arm, and its negative control ("omitting `gate_population_finding` from the shared function stores the fifth case's entry") has no red-to-green pair to demonstrate. The mechanism itself is fine; only the case's spelling is wrong, so the fix is to name a glob population (e.g. `pytest tests/test_missing_*.py`) or to state that the gate must name one — and to keep that path out of the entry's write paths, since `_population_covers_a_declared_write_path` exempts a declared write path.

response_events.note: §2's fifth case now names a glob population, pytest tests/test_missing_*.py, which gate_population_patterns keeps, and keeps that path out of the entry's write paths.
